name: The Room
tagline: What if the people who shaped how you think were still in the room?
statement: Books gave us access to great minds. The Room gives us a conversation with them.
summary: The Room is a source-grounded library of books, talks, interviews, notes, frameworks, and reusable AI instructions. It turns a static body of thought into a conversation without pretending that the person is literally present.
status: In preview on Vercel, behind its login

steps.title: The wall
steps.body: A wall of carved reliefs you can stand before and question. Each person has a From the wall label: biography, timeline, sources and one verbatim line. The Room's own brains were written from each person's SIGNAL file and every quote is re-verified at build time.

steps.title: The table
steps.body: Seat up to four from the wall and let them talk to each other. The stage draws the seats around a round top: two face each other across it, three put one at the head, four take the corners. The conversation then goes to the whole table: they answer in turn and to each other, keeping disagreement.
steps.alt: The table panel open over the wall: the wall in small, four seats, Ask the table.
steps.source: site/README.md (The table); the panel's own line: 'Seat up to four from the wall and let them talk to each other.'

steps.title: Ask them
steps.body: "I am here. Bring a question, or a name." The conversation is kept by Mnemosyne, keeper of the Room; stand before a person and they speak for themselves. A copy of the Room with no server behind it asks for an Anthropic API key, which stays in the browser only.
steps.alt: The Ask them panel open over the wall, with Mnemosyne's greeting.

steps.title: Carve a name
steps.body: The wall has room. Name someone who shaped how you think, and say why they belong here: a name, the years, what they did, in their words with the source, and why they belong in the Room.
steps.alt: A white plaster bust of Hannah Arendt on a paper ground.

steps.title: The rule of the Room
steps.body: A direct quote is the person's own language and must carry a source. A summary is a compact account of documented material. An application is present-day inference and must be labeled as such. Private journals, meetings, relationships and captures are not in the Room.
steps.alt: A white plaster bust of Dieter Rams on a paper ground.

source: The Room's own build photographed on 2026-10-22 (scripts/work/shoot.mjs): page titles and first words, typefaces and colours observed, the logo and pictures the pages show, the phone frames. Every word is qwarter.com's, the site's own or observed; nothing is written here. By hand (content/studies/_overrides/theroom.json): the words are the repository's own (journeynudger/theroom: README.md, site/README.md, site/data/i18n/en/ui.json, read 2026-10-22); the pictures its site/figures; photographed from its own build on 2026-10-22. The deployment Lorenzo linked is a Vercel preview behind Vercel's login, so there is no address to send a reader to yet.
brief: The wall is a web version of the Room: a wall of carved reliefs you can stand before and question, a From the wall label for each person with biography, timeline, sources and one verbatim line, an Ask them conversation kept by Mnemosyne, and Carve a name for nominating who belongs next. The table seats up to four people from the wall around a round table, facing each other, and lets them answer a question together and answer one another. The governing distinction: a direct quote is the person's own language and must carry a source; a summary is a compact account of documented material; an application is present-day inference and must be labeled as such.
